item.title: Mechanistic Insights Into Catechin Epimerization: Interplay of Deprotonation and Quinone Methide Stabilization
item.description:
Catechin epimerization is governed by the interplay between the acidity of the 4′-hydroxyl group and stabilization of a quinone methide intermediate. Experimental studies combined with DFT calculations reveal how B-ring substitution and C3 substituents control epimerization profiles, providing a molecular basis for understanding catechin transformations during thermal processing.


Catechin epimerization occurs during thermal processing of tea and can influence its bioactivity and nutritional properties. However, the structural factors governing epimerization behavior remain incompletely understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the effects of chemical structure on epimerization using native catechins and a series of model compounds under heating conditions relevant to food processing. The time-dependent changes in peak area ratios during epimerization and the equilibrium ratios were evaluated by HPLC analysis, and the observed trends were interpreted using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results demonstrate that epimerization is influenced by both the acidity (pK a) of the 4′-hydroxyl group and stability of the quinone methide intermediate, and is governed by the interplay between these factors. Electronic effects on the B-ring were found to influence deprotonation of the 4′-hydroxyl group, whereas intramolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions contributed to stabilization of the quinone methide intermediate. Substituents at the C3 position further influence both epimerization profile and equilibrium ratio through electronic and steric effects. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for catechin epimerization and provide insight into structure–reactivity relationships in polyphenolic systems undergoing quinone methide-mediated transformations.

item.title: Triptycene‐Fused Carbonyl‐Nitrogen Multiresonance Emitter for Efficient Green OLEDs With High Color Purity
item.description:
A novel carbonyl-nitrogen multiresonance emitter QA-TP is constructed by integrating steric triptycene substituents into the trans-quinacridone skeleton. The rigid 3D structure of QA-TP can effectively suppress molecular structural relaxation and restrict intermolecular stacking in the aggregated state, affording OLEDs with a high external quantum efficiency of 16.7% and a narrow full width at half maximum of 27 nm.


Carbonyl-nitrogen (CO-N) multiresonance (MR) materials have emerged as promising candidates for ultra-high-definition displays due to their high color purity, but they often suffer from severe spectral broadening in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), which hinders the construction of wide-color-gamut displays. Herein, we report a novel molecule QA-TP constructed by integrating bulky steric triptycene substituents into the CO-N-based trans-quinacridone skeleton. The rigid 3D structure of QA-TP can not only suppress molecular structural relaxation but also effectively restrict intermolecular stacking in the aggregated state, resulting in pure green emission with a narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM) value of 21 nm in toluene and 27 nm in doped film, both superior to the counterpart molecule QA-4Ph. Furthermore, hyperfluorescent OLED based on QA-TP emitter exhibits a satisfactory external quantum efficiency of 16.7% and a narrow FWHM of 27 nm, with CIE coordinates of (0.27, 0.66). These results verify the feasibility of directly incorporating rigid steric substituents into CO-N MR skeletons for developing narrowband emitters as well as OLEDs.

item.title: Iron‐Photocatalyzed Ligand‐to‐Metal Charge Transfer‐Driven Decarboxylative Giese‐Type Reactions Under Mild Conditions
item.description:
Iron-photocatalyzed LMCT enables decarboxylative hydroalkylation of Michael acceptors (Giese-type reaction) under mild conditions. Using tailored ligands and a sterically hindered very mild aniline base, diverse carboxylic acids efficiently couple with sensitive Michael acceptors, including maleimides. The method shows broad functional group tolerance and applicability to late-stage modification of bioactive molecules.


Iron-catalyzed ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) strategy provides a powerful platform for generating alkyl radicals from readily available carboxylic acids under mild photocatalytic conditions. Herein, we report an iron-photocatalyzed, LMCT-enabled decarboxylative Giese reaction that couples efficiently structurally diverse carboxylic acids with highly sensitive Michael acceptors. Key to this protocol is the use of a sterically hindered mild base in combination with tailored ligand systems. The method exhibits a broad substrate scope, including primary, secondary, and tertiary benzylic carboxylic acids, as well as challenging aliphatic carboxylic acids. Notably, it enables efficient functionalization of base-sensitive Michael acceptors, such as maleimides, which have shown limited compatibility in prior methodologies. Furthermore, the applicability of this protocol to bioactive molecules highlights its potential for late-stage modification. This work establishes a practical and complementary approach that expands the synthetic scope of iron-photocatalyzed decarboxylative Giese-type reactions.

item.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Axial Chiral Aryl Isoquinolines via N‐Directed 3d Metal Catalysts: A Perspective
item.description:
Axially chiral N-heterobiaryls are pivotal in catalysis, medicine, and materials. Traditional noble-metal or resolution routes suffer from high cost and limited scope. Nitrogen-directed 3d metal (Co, Ni) catalysis enables enantioconvergent functionalization via labile metallacycles. This perspective covers diverse coupling reactions, emphasizing axial epimerization, metal complementarity, and challenges in substrate generality, catalyst design, scalability, and application.


Axially chiral N-heterobiaryls are important structural motifs in asymmetric catalysis, medicinal chemistry, and chiral functional materials. Their enantioselective synthesis has traditionally relied on noble-metal catalysis or resolution-based strategies, which often suffer from high cost, limited modularity, and restricted coupling-partner scope. Recent advances in nitrogen-directed 3d metal catalysis have enabled the enantioconvergent functionalization of racemic N-heterobiaryl electrophiles. In these reactions, coordination of the heteroaryl nitrogen to cobalt or nickel promotes the formation of configurationally labile five-membered metallacyclic intermediates, allowing chiral ligands to control axial epimerization and subsequent bond formation through kinetic resolution or dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation. This perspective summarizes representative cobalt- and nickel-catalyzed strategies, including radical coupling, reductive conjugate addition, Grignard-type addition, Nozaki–Hiyama–Kishi-type addition, carbon–methoxy bond activation, carboxylation with carbon dioxide, carbon–phosphorus coupling, carbon–oxygen/carbon–sulfur coupling, and nucleophilic chlorination. Emphasis is placed on nitrogen-assisted axial epimerization, the complementary reactivity of cobalt and nickel, and future challenges in substrate generality, mechanism-guided catalyst design, scalability, and application-oriented synthesis.

item.title: Metal‐Free Construction of Alkyl Selenocyanates From Cyclic Sulfonium Salts, Selenium Powder, and Trimethylsilyl Cyanide
item.description:
A simple and efficient three-component ring-opening reaction of cyclic sulfonium salts with selenium powder and trimethylsilyl cyanide has been developed. This mild and convenient process successfully introduces the SeCN group into the sulfur-containing framework using selenium powder as the Se source.


A facile strategy has been developed for the synthesis of sulfur-containing alkyl selenocyanates through ring-opening reaction of cyclic sulfonium salts with Se powder and TMSCN. Under mild and convenient conditions, this protocol enables the introduction of the SeCN group into the sulfur-containing framework employing selenium powder as the selenium source.

item.title: Truncation of Samroiyotmycin: Tailored seco‐Acids as Novel Antimalaria Compounds
item.description:
Six truncated samroiyotmycin-derived antimalarials were synthesized by replacing the tosyloxazole unit with electron-deficient aryl groups. The most active seco-acid with EWG = 2 × CF3 outperformed the natural product SamA. Its enhanced activity supports a donor–acceptor interaction involving the electron-poor aryl unit, consistent with inhibition of hemozoin formation.


To facilitate synthetic access and address limitations associated with the tosyloxazole moiety in samroiyotmycin-derived antimalarials, six truncated analogs were prepared in combination with C-terminal methyl ester or carboxylic acid functionalities to mimic the electron-poor character of the parent motif. Biological evaluation identified the 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl-substituted seco-acid as the most potent derivative, surpassing tosyl-based reference compounds. The enhanced activity is consistent with a donor–acceptor interaction involving the electron-deficient aryl unit and supports its proposed role in the inhibition of hemozoin formation.

item.title: Hydroformylation of Olefins With Paraformaldehyde Catalyzed by a Rhodium(I)/Diphosphine/Diphosphoramidite System
item.description:
A new dual-ligand rhodium catalytic system based on [RhCl(cod)]2, BINAP or BIPHEP, and a diphosphoramidite ligand enables the hydroformylation of olefins using paraformaldehyde as a syngas surrogate. The system efficiently converts vinyl arenes, alkyl olefins, cyclopentene, and allyl acetate with high activity and regioselectivity.


A new dual-ligand rhodium catalytic system based on [RhCl(cod)]2 and BINAP or BIPHEP in combination with a readily accessible diphosphoramidite ligand has been developed for the hydroformylation of olefins using paraformaldehyde as a syngas surrogate. The catalytic system efficiently hydroformylates a broad range of substrates, including vinyl arenes, alkyl olefins, cyclopentene, and allyl acetate. High regioselectivity toward the linear aldehyde (up to 80%) was achieved for several aryl alkenes, with performances comparable to those obtained under conventional hydroformylation conditions. Hydroformylation of 1-decene revealed a strong influence of reaction temperature, reflecting competition between hydroformylation and olefin isomerization. 31P and 1H nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) studies identified a trigonal bipyramidal rhodium dicarbonyl hydride complex containing an equatorially coordinated diphosphoramidite ligand, providing evidence that this species is involved in the catalytic cycle. These results demonstrate the potential of inexpensive diphosphoramidite ligands for syngas-free rhodium-catalyzed hydroformylation.

item.title: Site‐Selective CH Alkylation of Pyrimidin‐2(1H)‐Ones Enabled by Visible‐Light‐Induced Organophotocatalysis
item.description:
H Alkylation of Pyrimidin-2(1H)-Ones Enabled by Visible-Light-Induced Organophotocatalysis"/>

An efficient photocatalytic site-selective method for introducing secondary and tertiary alkyl groups into N1-substituted pyrimidin-2(1H)-ones using alkyl trifluoroborate reagents was developed. This methodology significantly expands the accessible chemical space of densely decorated pyrimidin-2(1H)-ones and offers new opportunities for their broader application in medicinal chemistry. Mes, 2,4,6-trimethylphenyl.


A visible-light-induced photocatalytic method for regioselective CH alkylation at the electrophilic C4 and C6 positions of N1-substituted pyrimidin-2(1H)-ones using alkyl trifluoroborates, an acridinium-based photocatalyst, and potassium persulfate as oxidant is reported. The developed general protocol enables direct stepwise introduction of uncommon secondary and tertiary alkyl groups via a radical oxidative addition pathway, thereby expanding the accessible chemical space of substituted pyrimidines in a principally new direction. The impact of the nature of substituents at positions N1 and C5, as well as the effect of the acid additive, was investigated, providing a practical strategy for the synthesis of highly decorated heterocycles. The elaborated methodology predicted high suitability for both parallel synthesis and multigram-scale production of the target pyrimidones.

item.title: The Cyano‐Diels–Alder Reaction: From Nitrile Activation to Functional Molecular Architectures
item.description:
This Concept Article presents the evolution of the cyano-Diels–Alder reaction from its early examples to its current development as a valuable synthetic tool for the preparation of N-heterocycles, fused polycycles and functional chromophores, tracing the key breakthroughs that have transformed this underexplored transformation into a relevant platform for creating complex molecular architectures.


The cyano-Diels–Alder (c-DA) reaction represents an interesting yet underexplored variation of the classical DA reaction, hampered by the intrinsically poor dienophilic character of the nitrile group. In recent years, significant progress has been made in overcoming this limitation through rational activation strategies, including conjugation of the nitrile with strong electron-withdrawing substituents, intramolecular preorganization, Lewis acid coordination and the use of highly electron-deficient multicyano frameworks. This concept article highlights how these approaches have transformed the c-DA reaction from a poorly explored transformation into a valuable synthetic tool for the preparation of N-heterocycles and structurally complex polycyclic architectures. Particular attention is devoted to multicyano systems such as tetracyanobutadiene- and tetracyanoquinodimethane-derived scaffolds, in which cyano activation, molecular topology and cascade reactivity cooperate to unlock efficient intramolecular c-DA cycloadditions, leading to multifunctional chromophores. Altogether, the evolution of the c-DA reaction illustrates how a traditionally reluctant nitrile dienophile can be harnessed through molecular design to access increasingly sophisticated molecular architectures.

item.title: Fluorination of Alkyl‐Substituted Ylides With HBF4•Et2O
item.description:
The development of a rapid and efficient fluorination reaction of difluoroalkyl- and alkyl-substituted ylides employing HBF4•Et2O as the fluorinating agent is reported. This operationally simple protocol typically proceeds to full conversion within 5–30 min at room temperature or slightly above, affording a diverse array of monofluoroalkanes and trifluoromethylated alkanes in good to excellent yields. The exceptionally short reaction time, mild conditions, and use of a readily available fluorinating source render this method particularly attractive for applications that require rapid fluorine incorporation, such as the preparation of PET-CT tracers.


The development of a rapid and efficient fluorination reaction of difluoroalkyl- and alkyl-substituted ylides employing HBF4•Et2O as the fluorinating agent is reported. This operationally simple protocol typically proceeds to full conversion within 5–30 min at room temperature or slightly above, affording a diverse array of monofluoroalkanes and trifluoromethylated alkanes in good to excellent yields. The exceptionally short reaction time, mild conditions, and use of a readily available fluorinating source render this method particularly attractive for applications that require rapid fluorine incorporation, such as the preparation of PET-CT tracers.

item.title: Diels–Alder Versus Michael Adducts of 2‐Methylfuran and Maleate: Consecutive Synthetic Access to Both Product Types
item.description:
More than a century after Albrecht's original proposal, an unexpected synthetic relationship between the historically misassigned Michael adduct type and the genuine Diels–Alder product is revealed. Experimental and theoretical studies show that the Michael adduct is not formed directly from the diene and dienophile, but instead arises through catalytic rearrangement of the real cycloadduct.


Originally, the Diels–Alder reaction was not carried out, as one might assume, by Diels and Alder, but by Albrecht who reported this reaction already in 1906 and, thus, more than two decades earlier than Diels and Alder in their pioneer publication. However, Albrecht concluded a wrong structure for the product as he proposed a Michael adduct. In 1928, Diels and Alder then successfully identified the real structure and discovered the reaction class of [4 + 2] cycloaddition reactions, for which they were awarded Nobel Prize. Unexpectedly, we found in our experiments, for the conversion of 2-methylfuran and a maleate, that there is a synthetic relationship of the wrongly proposed and real types of Diels–Alder products. In detail, the Michael adduct is formed under catalytic conditions from the real Diels–Alder product through rearrangement. Subsequent theoretical studies revealed that the wrongly proposed structure is even more stable than the real Diels–Alder product and accordingly such Albrecht product should be formed in a thermodynamically controlled reaction. Thus, our results also suggest that the original proposal of Albrecht from 1906—which was corrected by Diels and Alder in 1928—was not entirely unrealistic. Although this synthesized Michael adduct is not obtained directly from the diene and dienophile, it, ironically, is formed from the real Diels–Alder product via this type of rearrangement reaction.

item.title: Introducing Amino Derivatives at the 3‐Position of Benzothiophene S,S‐Dioxide
item.description:
Aliphatic amines react directly with 3,5,6-tribromobenzothiophene S,S-dioxide via nucleophilic addition–elimination, whereas less nucleophilic aromatic amines require 5,6-dibromobenzothiophen-3-one S,S-dioxide. This activated core undergoes efficient, microwave-assisted condensation, providing a chromatography-free protocol to introduce amino groups at the 3-position.


The addition of aliphatic amines to 3,5,6-tribromobenzothiophene S,S-dioxide (3,5,6-Br-BTO) readily leads to substitution of the bromine atom at the 3-position via a nucleophilic addition–elimination pathway. Among aromatic amines, only the most nucleophilic derivatives undergo successful incorporation under these conditions. To broaden the scope to a wider range of amines, 3,5,6-Br-BTO was converted into 5,6-dibromobenzothiophenone S,S-dioxide (5,6-Br-BTKO). This activated intermediate enables efficient condensation under microwave irradiation, affording the corresponding amino derivatives without the need for chromatographic purification.

item.title: Metal‐Free Ligand‐Centered Radical Scavenging in Pyridine‐Modified Tetraaza Macrocycles
item.description:
Ligand-centered hydrogen-atom transfer in pyridinophane macrocycles generates delocalized radicals, with Py2N2 enabling cooperative captodative stabilization and enhanced DPPH• quenching.


Pyridine-modified tetraaza macrocycles are widely studied as ligand platforms for metal coordination, yet their intrinsic redox and radical reactivity in the absence of metals remains unclear. Here, we report the unexpected finding that pyridinophane Py2N2 and PyN3 macrocycles act as efficient metal-free radical scavengers toward the stable free radical 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH•). Systematic evaluation of substituent effects reveals distinct structure–reactivity relationships. PyN3 derivatives exhibit a linear dependence on electronic parameters, consistent with a donor-controlled regime, whereas Py2N2 macrocycles show a pronounced parabolic dependence on resonance and inductive effects, indicative of cooperative stabilization. 1H NMR spectroscopy supports the formation of a transient ligand–DPPH• encounter complex, followed by a rapid hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT). Density functional theory identifies the β-C–H position on the macrocyclic backbone as the thermodynamically preferred hydrogen-donor site. The resulting ligand-centered radical is formed with the Py2N2 and stabilized through delocalization across the macrocyclic framework, enabling a captodative-like electronic environment that is inaccessible to the PyN3 scaffold. Together, these findings establish a ligand-centered HAT mechanism governed by macrocyclic topology rather than metal coordination and highlight a previously unrecognized design principle for electronically tunable, metal-free macrocyclic radical scavengers.

item.title: Electrochemical α‐C(sp3)‐H Functionalization of Aryl Ketones via Thianthrenium Intermediates
item.description:
An electrochemical umpolung approach for the α-C(sp3)-H functionalization of aryl ketones via a sulfonium pool is described. The protocol proceeds at ambient temperature, allowing the use of oxidatively sensitive nucleophiles as reaction partners.


Electrochemical preparation and transformation of sulfonium ions have been paid increasing attention. Herein, we have developed an efficient electrochemical approach for the α-C(sp3)-H functionalization of aryl ketones via sulfonium salt pool. The reaction proceeds under constant current conditions at ambient temperature, avoiding the complex low-temperature operation typically required in the electrochemical generation of cation pools, and allowing the use of oxidatively sensitive nucleophiles, particularly ones with less positive potential than that of thianthrene as reaction partners, for downstream functionalization.

item.title: Regioselective Ring Opening of Non‐Activated Aziridines Using 2‐Substituted Indoles as Nucleophiles: Facile Synthesis of the Tryptophan Scaffold
item.description:
Facile, highly regio- and stereoselective ring-opening reactions of non-activated aziridines have been achieved using 2-substituted indoles in the presence of BF3 · OEt2 in acetonitrile at 80 °C. The resulting products serve as versatile substitutes for natural and unnatural tryptophan derivatives, thus offering nitrogen-containing scaffolds with potential in medicinal chemistry.


We report regio- and stereoselective ring-opening reactions of non-activated aziridines using 2-substituted indoles as nucleophiles in the presence of BF3·OEt2 in acetonitrile at 80°C. Under these conditions, unsubstituted indole led to dimerization, while 2-substituted indoles furnished α-amino esters in good to excellent yields. The reaction proceeds via Lewis acid activation of the aziridine, followed by indole attack at the less hindered C-3 carbon, and the regioselectivity of aziridine ring opening reaction is govern by both steric and electronic factors. The resulting products serve as intermediates for the synthesis of natural and unnatural tryptophan derivatives. This method offers a concise, selective, and broadly applicable route to nitrogen-containing scaffolds with potential in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Electrooxidative Synthesis of Benzoin Bis‐Ethers From Alkynes and Alcohols
item.description:
This mild transition-metal-free electrooxidation enables oxidative difunctionalization of alkynes to construct benzoin bis-ethers. It uses electrons as clean redox mediators under ambient conditions with broad substrate compatibility. Mechanistic studies confirm a radical cation pathway, and scaled-up synthesis verifies its synthetic practicability.


Herein, we present a mild and efficient electrochemical strategy for the synthesis of benzoin bis-ethers via oxidative difunctionalization of alkynes. This protocol proceeds under ambient conditions without requiring transition-metal catalysts or stoichiometric oxidants, utilizing electrons as a traceless redox mediator. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. A gram-scale experiments and product derivatization reactions highlight the practicality of this electrochemical strategy. Mechanistic investigations indicated a radical cation pathway, highlighting the utility of this sustainable approach for accessing valuable bis-ether frameworks.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed α‐Carbamoylation of Cyclic β‐Ketoesters
item.description:
Cu(II) salt-catalyzed reaction of cyclic β-ketoesters with isocyanates afforded hitherto inaccessible α-substituted β,β’-dicarbonyl amides possessing an all-carbon quaternary center.


A copper-catalyzed, base-free α-carbamoylation of cyclic β-ketoesters with isocyanates has been developed. While conventional base-promoted methods suffer from a spontaneous intramolecular rearrangement that leads to undesired imides, this protocol utilizes a Cu(OTf)2/bisoxazoline (BOX) catalytic system to effectively suppress the rearrangement pathway. The reaction provides efficient access to various α-substituted β,β′-dicarbonyl amides bearing an all-carbon quaternary center in high yields with a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance.

item.title: Development of Sandwich‐Compound‐Based Planar‐Chiral Six‐Membered Unsaturated N‐Heterocyclic Carbene Ligands
item.description:
Sandwich-compound-based planar-chiral six-membered unsaturated NHC ligands were developed. Notably, a Rh complex coordinated by an NHC ligand bearing an η5-cyclopentadienyl–cobalt–η4-tetraphenylcyclobutadiene core was synthesized and confirmed to catalyze the asymmetric ring-opening reaction of benzonorbornadiene with N-methylaniline (61% yield, 56% ee).


Sandwich-compound-based planar-chiral six-membered unsaturated N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands were developed. Their formation was indirectly confirmed through trapping experiments in which carbene precursors were reacted with sulfur or [RhCl(cycloocta-1,5-diene (cod))]2 in the presence of a base (t-BuOK or lithium bis(trimethylsilyl)amide (LiHMDS)). Determining the Tolman electronic parameter of the Rh dicarbonyl complex [RhCl(CO)2((R p)-4b)] revealed slightly stronger electron-donating ability (2045 cm–1) than representative classic diaminocarbenes (e.g., SIMes: 2051 cm–1). Furthermore, the structure of the NHC ligand (R p)-4b was unambiguously confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis of the related complex [RhI(cod)((R p)-4b)], and its utility as a chiral ligand was preliminarily demonstrated in the Rh-catalyzed asymmetric ring-opening reaction of oxabenzonorbornadiene with N-methylaniline (61% yield, 56% enantiomeric excess (ee)).

item.title: The Chemical Sciences Towards a Sustainable Future: Update on an Enduring Collaboration With Henning Hopf
item.description:
The C4S group (L to R: Goverdhan Mehta, Alain Krief, Stephen Matlin, Henning Hopf) at a workshop in India in 2019.


Henning Hopf was a co-founder and, for more than a decade, has been one of four core members of the group ‘Chemists for Sustainability’ (C4S) within the International Organization for Chemical Sciences in Development. During this period C4S served as a think tank and commentator, opening windows into new areas, providing perspectives for chemists into and beyond the mainstream activities of the discipline in education, research, and practice. Of especial significance has been the C4S proposal made in 2016 to introduce systems thinking into chemistry, which has gained considerable traction and catalysed deep-seated reforms in chemistry education. The group has itself used the systems thinking tool to examine how chemistry can strengthen its engagement in the contemporary context of global challenges across diverse areas of science, including health, environmental sustainability, and the interfaces of science, policy, and health. This has included such diverse domains as human security, equity, diversity, and inclusion, resilience and the world of science publishing, where the value of systems-based approaches to making connections of local and global significance has been exemplified.

item.title: The Design and Synthesis of High‐Performance Two‐Photon Absorbing Fluorophores With Large Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections and High Fluorescence Emission Quantum Yields
item.description:
The structural characteristics that reduce the fluorescence quantum yield of two-photon absorbing fluorophores have been discussed, and the recent progress in the development of high-performance two-photon absorbing fluorophores with large two-photon absorption cross sections and high fluorescence emission quantum yields have been reviewed.


The attainment of a large two-photon absorption (2 PA) cross section and a high fluorescence emission quantum yield are crucial goal in molecular design of two-photon absorbing fluorophores. However, the intrinsic modulation guidelines have rarely been revealed. Our review offers valuable insights into the photophysical properties of several organic fluorophores in the last 5 years and provides rational guidelines for the design and synthesis of organic fluorophores with both large 2 PA cross section and high fluorescence emission quantum yield.

item.title: Selective N‐Functionalization of Pyrazoles
item.description:
This review traces the evolution of regioselective N-functionalization strategies for pyrazoles, a key class of nitrogen heterocycles widely used in medicinal chemistry. Due to rapid tautomerism, N-functionalization often lacks selectivity, leading to poor and unpredictable regioisomeric outcomes. Recent advances in transition-metal catalysis, directing-group, radical, and skeletal-editing strategies have improved control and expanded access to diverse substitution patterns.


Pyrazoles are five-membered heteroarenes that contain two neighboring nitrogen atoms and appear in diverse functional molecule classes. One nitrogen contributes a lone-pair to the aromatic π-system, while the lone-pair of the other lies orthogonal. However, easy interconversion between tautomers of N─H pyrazoles occurs and the two forms lie close in energy to each other. As a consequence, N-functionalization reactions most commonly lead to mixtures of products in what is a well-known synthetic challenge. Demand for selective, efficient alternatives has prompted innovation of new, diverse synthetic strategies which can overcome this problem. In this review, we focus on the most recent developments in this field.

item.title: Regio‐ and Stereoselective Synthesis of Spirooxindole–Pyrrolidine Hybrids Through 1,3‐Dipolar Cycloaddition: The Development of Potent α‐Glucosidase Inhibitors
item.description:
A novel series of spirooxindole–pyrrolidine hybrids was synthesized via a regio- and stereoselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition. Bromine-substituted derivatives showed high α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Structural elucidation confirmed stereochemistry, revealing that the electronic nature of arylimine substituents influences diastereoselectivity and provides insights for designing more potent future inhibitors.


A novel series of spirooxindole–pyrrolidine hybrids was synthesized and evaluated for their potential as α-glucosidase inhibitors. These compounds were obtained via a regio- and stereoselective 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition reaction between arylimines and an isatin-derived alkene. Structural elucidation by NMR spectroscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction enabled unambiguous stereochemical assignment and provided insight into the diastereoselectivity of the reaction. Furthermore, the stereochemical outcome was found to be influenced by the electronic nature of the substituents on the arylimine moiety, offering valuable insight into the reaction mechanism. Among the synthesized compounds, bromine-substituted analogues exhibited α-glucosidase inhibitory activity over 12-fold greater than that of the reference drug acarbose, highlighting their potential as lead compounds for the development of next-generation inhibitors.

item.title: A Modular and Scalable Synthesis of Imidazole‐Embedded Crown Ethers and Evaluation of Their Cation Binding Properties
item.description:
Imidazole-containing crown ethers were synthesized through a concise and scalable strategy enabling access to a homologous macrocyclic series. Binding studies reveal that alkali metal recognition remains comparable to that of classical crown ethers and related analogs, while the enhanced hydrogen-bond acceptor ability of the imidazole unit promotes exceptionally high pseudorotaxane formation with dibenzylammonium hexafluorophosphate.


A modular and scalable synthetic route to imidazole-containing crown ethers has been developed, enabling access to a homologous series of macrocycles ranging from 15- to 24-membered rings. Central to the strategy is the concise synthesis of 2,4-bis(hydroxymethyl)imidazole, obtained selectively in three steps and with a 36% overall yield without the need for protecting-group manipulations. The cation-binding properties of the imidazole-containing crown ethers toward sodium and potassium hexafluorophosphate salts were studied, showing binding affinities comparable to those of classical crown ethers, while exhibiting donor properties intermediate between ether- and pyridine-containing analogs. The enhanced basicity and hydrogen-bond acceptor ability of the imidazole unit had a more pronounced effect on secondary ammonium recognition. In particular, a highly stable pseudorotaxane with dibenzylammonium hexafluorophosphate could be formed with an association constant of approximately 1 × 104 M−1 in acetonitrile. This value ranks among the highest reported for crown ether-based pseudorotaxane systems under comparable conditions.

item.title: Counterion Effects in Decatungstate Photocatalysis
item.description:
Decatungstate photocatalysis is often discussed from an anion-centered perspective, treating the counterion as a passive charge-balancing species. This review highlights that counterion identity can instead profoundly influence catalyst solubility, ion pairing, aggregation, stability, substrate accessibility, and catalytic performance. Counterion engineering therefore offers a strategic and underexplored avenue for tuning decatungstate photocatalysis across homogeneous and heterogeneous systems.


Photocatalysis with decatungstate ([W10O32]4−, DT) is a versatile platform for hydrogen-atom-transfer (HAT)-mediated CH functionalization under mild conditions. Decatungstate is valued for its ability to abstract hydrogen from strong aliphatic, benzylic, allylic, and α-heteroatom CH bonds. Its efficiency is often attributed to the excited-state reactivity of [W10O32]4− and substrate CH bond strength, but this view neglects the vital role of counterions, which are integral to the catalytic system and influence performance. In solution, DT forms dynamic ion-paired ensembles where counterions affect solubility, substrate access, ion pairing, aggregation, and photostability. These factors impact activity, selectivity, productivity, and robustness. This perspective discusses counterion effects across various systems, including sodium, tetrabutylammonium, phosphonium derivatives, ionic liquids, and immobilized platforms. It highlights counterions as active components that govern catalytic parameters, aiding better catalyst design and system development.

item.title: Rh(II)‐Catalyzed Cascade Cyclization Between Azidobenzoic Acids and Diazopyrazolones for Construction of Spirobenzo[d][1,3]oxazin‐4‐ones
item.description:
Under the catalysis of Rh(II)2(OAc)4, Cu(I)OTf and iso Pr-PHOX L13, azidobenzoic acids react with diazopyrazolones in a rhodium-carbenoid- and rhodium-nitrenoid-mediated dual-insertion cascade cyclization. This transformation proceeds smoothly to deliver the target spirobenzo[d][1,3]oxazin-4-ones in reasonable yields.


In the presence of Rh(II)2(OAc)4 (10 mol%), Cu(I)OTf (10 mol%), and iso Pr-PHOX L13 (20 mol%) in 1,2-dichloroethane at 80 °C, the cascade cyclization between azidobenzoic acids and diazopyrazolones proceeded readily and furnished spirobenzo[d][1,3]oxazin-4-ones in reasonable chemical yields. The chemical structure of one compound has been confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis, and the others are suggested by inference.

item.title: Unified Approach for the Synthesis of Close Analogues of Reverse‐Prenylated Hexahydropyrrolo Indole Alkaloids
item.description:
A simple, modular, and unified strategy for the synthesis of reverse-prenylated hexahydropyrrolo indole alkaloids has been developed. An unusual retrosynthetic disconnection allows for the late introduction of a side chain, which distinguishes many members of this class of natural products. Therefore, it is possible to efficiently synthesise different congeners and, in particular, various natural product analogues from the same single intermediate.


A straightforward and unified synthetic approach to reverse-prenylated hexahydropyrrolo indole alkaloids has been established. It uses an unusual disconnection which allows for the late stage introduction of the side chain of one of the amino acids — a crucial element of structural diversity in this class of natural products. Accordingly, the obligatory tryptophan is condensed to glycine (as the minimal second amino acid), followed by a regio- and stereoselective introduction of the reverse prenyl group with concomitant formation of the hexahydropyrrolo indole substructure. The resulting general framework is finally alkylated at the α-position of the glycine to formally introduce the amino acid side chain. The presented strategy is particularly suited for the synthesis of a small focused library of close natural product analogues differing in the second variable amino acid substructure. In particular, the introduction of functionalised, rare, or unnatural and d-amino acids is straightforward. The viability of the concept was demonstrated by a short synthesis of epi-Fructigenine A and dehydro-Brevicompanine B. Notably, the two natural product analogues are accessible in only 3 and 2 steps, respectively, from the same general precursor. It is also worth mentioning that a new N-protecting group was developed as part of the research project presented.

item.title: FeIII‐Mediated Synthesis of Azaspirodienones via Ipso‐Radical Cyclization of Ugi–4CR Adducts
item.description:
An efficient two-step protocol for the synthesis of azaspirodienones via Fe-mediated ipso-radical cyclization of Ugi adducts has been developed. This methodology provides rapid access to these privileged spirocyclic architectures under mild conditions, offering a practical and versatile approach to generating structurally complex molecules with potential biological relevance.


A concise and operationally simple two-step protocol for the efficient synthesis of azaspirodienones through FeIII-mediated ipso-radical cyclization of Ugi adducts has been developed. The strategy combines the versatility of multicomponent Ugi reactions with the synthetic power of radical cyclization, enabling rapid construction of structurally complex and medicinally relevant spirocyclic frameworks from readily accessible starting materials.

item.title: Recent Progress in Mechanochemical Organocatalysis
item.description:
Recent progress in the application of organocatalytic transformations under mechanochemical conditions shows excellent compatibility of these two concepts. Both covalent and noncovalent activation modes of asymmetric organocatalysis can be advantageously realized using mechanochemical activation. Furthermore, several nonstereoselective transformations were shown to benefit from mechanochemistry too.


Mechanochemical activation has emerged as a powerful enabling strategy for sustainable organic synthesis, offering reduced solvent consumption, shorter reaction times, and access to reactivity patterns that may differ from conventional solution chemistry. This review summarizes recent progress in mechanochemical organocatalysis, with particular emphasis on asymmetric transformations performed under solvent-free or liquid-assisted grinding conditions. After outlining the historical development of the field, including early grindstone chemistry, liquid-assisted grinding, and pioneering ball-milling studies, we discuss representative advances in covalent and noncovalent organocatalysis. Proline-derived catalysts, peptides, primary and secondary amines, iminium catalysts, hydrogen-bond donors, squaramides, thioureas, and Brønsted acids have enabled efficient aldol, Michael, Mannich, cycloaddition, annulation, cascade, and heterofunctionalization reactions, often with high yields and stereoselectivities. Recent nonstereoselective applications, including ring-opening polymerizations, multicomponent reactions, biomass-derived condensations, and heterocycle syntheses, further demonstrate the expanding scope of this approach. The reviewed examples highlight mechanochemistry as more than an alternative mixing method; it provides a distinct reaction environment that can influence catalyst performance, chemoselectivity, and selectivity. Remaining challenges include mechanistic understanding, scalability, reproducibility, and rational additive selection.

item.title: One‐Pot Stereoselective Synthesis of Substituted E‐Furan‐3(2H)‐Imines From Propargyl Amines and Acyl Chlorides via Pd/Cu‐ and t‐BuOK‐Catalyzed Sequential Steps
item.description:
One-pot stereoselective synthesis of substituted E-furan-3(2H)-imines from propargyl amines and acyl chlorides via Pd/Cu- and t-BuOK-catalyzed sequential steps has been developed. The synthesis was proved to proceed via the base-catalyzed rearrangement of the intermediate acylpropargyl amines, which can be separately employed as starting materials to stereoselectively provide the same E-furan-3(2H)-imines with equal efficiency.


A new family of aromatic (heteroaromatic) propargyl amines (available from ketimines and acetylene gas), after the reaction with (hetero)aroyl chlorides (CuI/PdCl2/Ph3P/Et3N, 40–45 °C, toluene, 2–3 h) and sequential treatment with t-BuOK (room temperature, 5–8 h), stereoselectively delivered polysubstituted E-furan-3(2H)-imines in up to 72% yields. The latter were proved to be formed from the initially generated intermediate acylpropargyl amines, which underwent the unique base-catalyzed rearrangement proceeding via the intermediate aziridines, products of intramolecular addition of nitrogen-centered anion to the triple bond. In the intermediate aziridines, the cleavage of the C─N bond occurs with simultaneous formation of the C─O bond followed by deep restructuring to give the final products.

item.title: Molybdooxaziridine Catalysis: Synthesis of α‐Hydroxysulfones From Styrenes Through an ATRA Process
item.description:
This work has discovered that molybdooxaziridine catalysts promote the hydroxysulfonation of substituted α-methyl-styrenes using N-Ts-hydroxylamine as the nitrogen source. An atom-transfer-radical-addition mechanism involving the stepwise addition of Ts and hydroxy radicals takes place. The reaction works with great selectivities, and it is rather ideal for the facile functionalization of substituted alkenes.


Herein, we report the MoO2Dipic-promoted hydroxysulfonation of α-methyl-styrenes using N-Ts-hydroxylamine as the quantitative source of N. The reaction works with high yields and stereoselectivites for α-methyl-styrenes with a wide variety of substitution patterns. An atom-transfer-radical-addition mechanism involving the formation of a molybdooxaziridine complex as the active catalyst, then Ts radical addition, followed by hydroxy radical addition as the rate-determining step has been proposed. Initial kinetic and mechanistic data indicate initial mono-functionalization without NO radical addition and provide evidence for the proposed mechanism.

item.title: Resolution Approaches Toward Enantiopure Planar Chiral 7‐bromo‐4‐hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane
item.description:
This work describes access to both enantiomers of planar chiral 7-bromo-4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane through direct resolution of the racemate using an L-isoleucine-derived chiral auxiliary or through resolution of 4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane, followed by regioselective bromination.


The resolution of racemic planar chiral 7-bromo-4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane was first achieved through the formation of epimeric esters derived from N-phtalimide L-isoleucine. Two successive crystallization steps, followed by saponification, enabled the isolation of the (R P) enantiomer in enantiopure form (ee > 99%) and in 33% overall yield. In contrast, the opposite (S P) enantiomer could only be obtained with a moderate enantiomeric excess of 46%. To overcome this limitation, an alternative strategy based on an early-stage resolution process was developed. This method relied on the separation of the two enantiomers of racemic 4-hydroxy [2.2]paracyclophane by high-performance liquid chromatography with a Daicel Chiralpack IA column, followed by regioselective bromination. This sequence produced both enantiomers of the targeted disubstituted [2.2]paracyclophane, which were isolated in pure enantiomeric form and obtained in good overall yields.

item.title: Photocatalytic Synthesis of Indoles via NHC‐Boryl Radical Cascade Cyclization of 2‐Vinylaryl Isocyanides
item.description:
A thiol/photoredox dual catalytic strategy enables the synthesis of C2-borylated indoles from 2-vinylaryl isocyanides and NHC-boranes under visible-light irradiation. The transformation proceeds through NHC-boryl radical addition and intramolecular cyclization, providing the desired indoles with broad substrate scope and excellent regioselectivity.


A thiol/photoredox dual catalytic protocol has been developed for the synthesis of C2-borylated indoles from 2-vinylaryl isocyanides and NHC-boranes. Under visible-light irradiation, NHC-boryl radicals are generated in situ and undergo addition to the isocyanide unit, followed by intramolecular cyclization to deliver the indole framework. The method proceeds under mild conditions, exhibits good functional-group tolerance, and affords the products with high regioselectivity. Gram-scale experiments and the synthesis of tri-indolyl NHC-borane further demonstrate the synthetic utility of this protocol.

item.title: 1,2‐Dihydroxyanthraquinone, 6,7‐Dihydroxyisobenzofuranone and 7,8‐Dihydroxyquinolinone Derivatives as Ligands for the Self‐Assembly of Hierarchically Formed Lithium‐Bridged Titanium(IV) Helicates
item.description:
Catechol-based annulated aromatics with carbonyl units are ideal ligands for the formation of titanium(IV) containing lithium-bridged hierarchical helicates. They allow for the first time the use of amide units to obtain the dimeric helicate-type complexes.


1,2-Dihydroxyanthraquinone, 6,7-dihydroxyisobenzofuranone, and 7,8-dihydroxyquinolinone derivatives are fused aromatics with a catechol and a neighboring carbonyl unit (ketone, ester, amide). Those compounds act as complex ligands and form hierarchical helicates Li[Li3Ti2(L)6]. Due to the geometric fixation of the carbonyl unit, for the first time the hierarchical helicates can be obtained even with amide moieties as carbonyl.

item.title: Stereoselective Construction of Benzo‐Fused Tetrahydropyrrole Thiazines From Saccharin
item.description:
Saccharin was used as a template to construct a series of 10a-substituted, benzo-fused, pyrrolo thiazinone dioxides. Thereafter, diastereo-divergent 10-keto reduction gave either diastereomeric alcohol in a process that did not rely on the substituent at 10a's identity. Finally, in the case of R = H, a chemoselective reduction was employed to excise the sulfonyl group.


Five Gabriel–Colman-derived 3-acyl substituted benzo[e][1,2]thiazine 1,1-dioxides were converted into the corresponding benzo[e]pyrrolo[1,2-b][1,2]thiazine 5,5-dioxides via base-promoted alkylation with 1,3-dibromopropane. Thereafter, diastereo-divergent conversion of their 10-keto functionality is detailed. Hydrogenation (H2 and Pd/C), or reduction with NaBH4, led to selective generation of the cis-β-hydroxy acyl diastereomers, whereas treatment with acidic zinc gave trans-β-hydroxy acyl products. Finally, as a means to access 2-benzyl-substituted pyrrolidine, lithium-liquid ammonia-mediated reductive sulfonyl excision of both types of 10-hydroxy benzo[e]pyrrolo[1,2-b][1,2]thiazine 5,5-dioxide diastereomer was examined. Use of excess lithium led to reduction of both the sulfonyl group and the benzylic alcohol. Conversely, use of less lithium efficiently removed the sulfonyl group but left the benzylic alcohol group intact.

item.title: Diastereoselective Synthesis of a Medicinally Significant Cis−1,1,3‐Trisubstituted Cyclopentane Derivative through Epoxide Ring Opening
item.description:
A scalable synthesis of a pharmaceutically relevant cis-1,1,3-trisubstituted cyclopentane derivative is reported, evolving from a racemic approach to a diastereoselective scale-up process and ultimately an asymmetric route. Key steps include stereoselective Michael addition, Corey–Chaykovsky epoxidation, and controlled epoxide ring opening, as supported by density functional theory mechanistic studies.


We report the synthesis of a pharmaceutically relevant cis-1,1,3-trisubstituted cyclopentane derivative through the evolution of a racemic route into a robust diastereoselective scale-up process and, ultimately, an asymmetric synthesis. The optimized strategy features a sequence of stereoselective transformations, including a Michael addition, Corey–Chaykovsky epoxide formation, and controlled epoxide ring opening. Emphasis is placed on the diastereoselective ring opening of a key spiro-epoxide intermediate, which was investigated experimentally and rationalized by density functional theory calculations. The diastereoselective route proved reliable on multi-hundred-gram scale, consistently delivering high yields, while the asymmetric variant enabled access to the desired cis-diastereomer with excellent enantio and diastereocontrol on a milligram-scale. This work provides a practical and scalable approach to a synthetically challenging cyclopentane motif of medicinal relevance.

item.title: Morita–Baylis–Hillman Reaction of N‐Aryl Acrylamide, with a Vast Substrate Scope: Importance of NH Proton in Reaction Mechanism
item.description:
H Proton in Reaction Mechanism"/>

The MBH reaction of N-aryl acrylamide has been reported with an unprecedented substrate scope. The vital role that the N H proton plays for proton transfer in the reaction mechanism was also uncovered.


The Morita–Baylis–Hillman (MBH) reaction involves the coupling of a Michael acceptor with an electrophile. The MBH adduct is a heavily decorated synthetic template with numerous applications. Unfortunately, acrylamide, being a fundamental Michael acceptor, has been left out of the MBH domain. With limited reports or indirect methods to access acrylamide-derived MBH adducts, their further applications remain unexplored. Herein, we report the MBH reaction of N-aryl acrylamide with an unprecedented substrate scope. Extensive optimisations were carried out. For substrate scope, wide-ranging variations were successfully carried out at the aldehyde and acrylamide ends. Additives in the form of protecting groups and functional groups were also evaluated effectively. The reactions were conducted, mostly in solvent-free conditions, making it a green protocol. With control experiments, we also uncover the vital role that the N H proton plays for proton transfer and rate acceleration in the reaction mechanism.

item.title: An Iodine‐Mediated [3+2+1] Povarov Strategy for Accessing Pyridocoumarins With Tunable Solvatochromic Properties and Serum Albumin‐Binding Ability
item.description:
Pyridocoumarin derivatives are synthesized through [3+2+1] Povarov type cycloaddition reaction using acetophenones, 6-aminocoumarine, and styrenes under I2-DMSO condition. Fluorescence solvatochromic response of representative synthesized system and their interaction behavior with bovine serum albumin has also been investigated.


Being a fused system having both coumarin and quinoline moieties, pyridocoumarins exhibit various biological activities such as antiallergic, antidiabetic, analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial, etc. Three component Povarov type [3 + 2 + 1] cycloaddition reaction between acetophenones, 6-aminocoumarin and styrenes has been developed under I2-DMSO condition to synthesize a series of 2-benzyol-4-phenyl substituted fused pyridocoumarins. The reaction mechanism proceeds via Kornblum oxidation of acetophenone to result phenylglyoxal, which later undergoes Povarov type of reaction to yield the desired product. Fluorescence solvatochromic response of representative synthesized system and their interaction behavior with bovine serum albumin has also been investigated to highlight the photochemical and biomedical application potency of this class of compounds.

item.title: Rhodium‐Catalyzed Successive [3 + 2]/[4 + 2] Annulation of 2‐(Acetylamino)pyridines With Alkynes to Construct Tetracyclic Pyridopyrroloisoquinoline Frameworks
item.description:
Efficient construction of tetracyclic fused heterocycles has been achieved by rhodium-catalyzed double C–H annulation of 2-(acetylamino)pyridines with diarylacetylenes involving deacetylation. It has been revealed that the combination of rhodium and silver catalysts effectively promotes the deacetylation step.


The rhodium-catalyzed double dehydrogenative annulation of 2-(acetylamino)pyridines with two molecules of diarylacetylenes through deacetylation proceeds smoothly to produce pyrido[3′,2′:4,5]pyrrolo[2,1-a]isoquinoline derivatives. The annulation method provides a straightforward synthetic route to tetracyclic or pentacyclic fused heteroarenes from simple, readily available substrates.

item.title: Mechanistic Dichotomy in Enantioselective Pd‐Catalyzed Alkylation of Pyrroles With Diazoesters
item.description:
Ligand-controlled mechanistic divergence controls the Pd-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of pyrroles with diazoesters. While bipyridine ligands promote a conventional metal-carbene pathway, bipyridine-N,N′-dioxide ligands redirect catalysis through electrophilic CH metalation before carbene transfer. These findings reveal how ligand design can fundamentally alter catalytic mechanisms and reaction outcomes.


A palladium-catalyzed enantioselective CH alkylation of pyrroles with diazoesters using axially chiral bipyridine-N,N′-dioxide ligands is reported. The transformation provides direct access to enantioenriched pyrrole derivatives under mild conditions and expands the limited repertoire of asymmetric Pd-catalyzed pyrrole functionalization. Crucially, comparative studies reveal that bipyridine-N,N′-dioxide and bipyridine ligands operate through fundamentally different catalytic manifolds. Kinetic analysis, reactivity experiments, and product distribution studies indicate that N-oxide ligands divert the reaction from a conventional metal-carbene-initiated pathway to a mechanism involving electrophilic CH metalation followed by carbene transfer and protonation. These findings demonstrate that subtle ligand modification can alter the mechanistic pathway in Pd-catalyzed reactions of diazo compounds, paving the way to mechanistically informed strategies for asymmetric CH functionalization of electron-rich heterocycles.

item.title: Stereoselective and Diastereospecific Aminosilylation and Hydrosilylation of Heterobicyclic Alkenes by Copper Catalysis Under Mild Conditions
item.description:
An efficient and straightforward methodology for the stereoselective and diastereospecific aminosilylation and hydrosilylation of heterobicyclic norbornene derivatives is introduced. The mild conditions enable the functionalization of norbornene substrates with broad functional-group tolerance. The versatility of the protocol across a diverse range of substrates is demonstrated, and various silylation reagents are used to synthesize silylated products with high selectivity. This study provides insight into the selective modification of norbornene-based compounds, expanding their potential for application in synthetic chemistry.


An efficient and straightforward methodology for a stereoselective and diastereospecific aminosilylation and hydrosilylation of heterobicyclic norbornene derivatives is introduced. Emphasizing mild reaction conditions, the approach enables the functionalization of norbornene substrates with broad functional-group tolerance. The versatility of the protocol across a diverse range of substrates is demonstrated, and various silylation reagents to achieve highly selective silylation products are employed. This work provides valuable insights into the selective modification of norbornene-based compounds, expanding their potential applications in synthetic chemistry.

item.title: Organophotoredox‐Catalyzed Oxyalkylation–Peroxidation of Alkenes With Ethers and Tert‐Butyl Hydroperoxide
item.description:
An organophotoredox-catalyzed three-component peroxidation of alkenes with ethers and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) has been disclosed.


We report a visible-light-induced three-component peroxidation of alkenes with ethers and tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP) using Rhodamine B as an organophotoredox catalyst. This environmentally friendly protocol provides efficient access to a variety of multisubstituted tert-butyl peroxides. The resulting tert-butylperoxy group can be selectively converted into carbonyl or hydroxyl groups under mild conditions, highlighting the synthetic utility of this peroxidation strategy.

item.title: DMDM Hydantoin as C1 Precursor for Solvent‐Controlled C‐3 Hydroxymethylation and Methylenation of Imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridines
item.description:
A metal-free, additive-free, facile solvent-controlled selective hydroxymethylation and methylenation of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines using DMDM hydantoin as a C1 source under mild conditions has been developed.


A facile solvent-controlled selective hydroxymethylation and methylenation of imidazo[1,2-a]pyridines using DMDM hydantoin as a C1 source under mild conditions has been developed. The reaction yielded good-to-excellent yields for various imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine derivatives. The key features of this protocol are metal-free, oxidant-free, and operational simplicity. Further modification of the hydroxymethyl group was demonstrated, enabling the synthesis of structurally diverse imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine frameworks.

item.title: Synthesis, Characterization, and Antibacterial Properties of Novel Fluorene‐Triazole Hybrids
item.description:
The synthesis and characterization of five fluorene-triazole hybrids and their triazolium salts, as well as the antibacterial properties of the latter.


Five new fluorene-based triazoles were obtained through copper (I) catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition. These were subsequently converted to the corresponding triazolium salts with the use of methyl iodide. The new derivatives were characterized by NMR, IR, UV, and mass spectrometry. Four new crystal structures, two triazoles and two triazolium salts, were recorded and discussed. Moreover, all ten derivatives display photoluminescent properties. These were analyzed, and it was found that the new triazolium salts display large Stokes shifts of around 120 nm. The triazolium salts were also tested for antibacterial properties against Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and Gram-negative Escherichia coli and were shown to possess bactericidal properties, while two of the five tested derivatives displayed lower minimum inhibitory concentration values than the reference antibiotic Levofloxacin.

item.title: Synthesis of Functionalized Pyrrolo[1,2‐a]pyrimidin‐4‐one via Copper‐Catalyzed Domino Annulation/Ring Expansion
item.description:
A copper-catalyzed intramolecular annulation strategy was developed for the synthesis of pyrrolo[1,2-a]pyrimidinone scaffolds using oxime acetates and α,β-unsaturated carbonyl pyrrole scaffolds.


A copper-catalyzed annulation of oxime acetates with pyrrole scaffolds bearing α,β-unsaturated carbonyl groups was developed for the construction of pyrrolo[1,2-a]pyrimidinone scaffolds. The key steps in this cascade process include a [3 + 2] spiroannulation, in situ oxidation, followed by rearrangement.

item.title: Front Cover: Stereoselective Construction of Benzo‐Fused Tetrahydropyrrole Thiazines From Saccharin (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 33/2026)
item.description: The Front Cover highlights how a saccharin-derived ketone can be reduced by using complementary, highly diastereoselective processes. Acidic Zn leads to the alcohol product from Re-facial attack; whereas NaBH4 or H2, Pd/C, produces the alcohol product of Si-facial attack. The Dublin-Area-Rapid-Transit (DART) trains illustrate these different destinations… sweetly done! More information can be found in the Research Article by P. Evans and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/ejoc.70678).

item.title: Light‐Induced, Three‐Component Synthesis of Ketones: A Decade Review
item.description:
Light-induced three-component reactions have emerged as a powerful strategy for ketone synthesis. This review is organized by the carbon skeletons. Alkenes, alkynes, simple ketones, phenols, and [1.1.1] propellane serve as versatile building blocks, with O2 (even air), H2O, H2O2, TBHP, CO, aldehydes, and simple ketones as key carbonyl oxygen sources.


The past decade has witnessed remarkable advances in light-induced, three-component ketone synthesis, yet a systematic and updated overview remains absent since the last relevant review in 2020. This review fills that gap by providing a comprehensive survey of the field from 2015 to 2025, with a particular focus on substrate diversity and mechanistic analysis. We organize the literature by the carbon skeletons, including alkenes, alkynes, simple ketones, phenols, and [1.1.1]propellane. We also systematically analyze the role of carbonyl oxygen sources, such as O2/air, H2O, H2O2, TBHP, CO, aldehydes, and ketones. By emphasizing mechanistic details for each transformation, this review not only consolidates scattered knowledge but also aims to guide future reaction design and inspire new synthetic strategies in sustainable ketone synthesis.

item.title: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of (−)‐ and (+)‐Dihydromethysticin With Computational Insights Into CYP2B6 Binding
item.description:
A concise enantioselective total synthesis of both dihydromethysticin enantiomers ((+)- and (−)-DHM) is achieved via an Evans syn-aldol strategy that establishes the C-6 stereocenter of the α-pyrone core. The concise route provides efficient access to enantiopure (+)-DHM or (−)-DHM and enables further investigation of its interaction with CYP2B6.


The pharmacological potential of (+)-dihydromethysticin [(+)-DHM, 1] from kava kava, as a strong inhibitor of methadone metabolism, is currently constrained by the absence of a direct, scalable, and stereoselective synthesis. Isolation from natural sources is limited by low yields and difficult purification. The requirement for the nonnatural enantiomer, (−)-DHM, to investigate biological activity necessitates a robust synthetic approach. To overcome this, we report an efficient, enantioselective total synthesis of both DHM enantiomers. Our strategy uses an Evans syn-aldol reaction as the pivotal chirality-inducing step, enabling the stereospecific installation of the C-6 absolute configuration within the α-pyrone core via readily available chiral oxazolidinone antipodes. Subsequent transformations of aldol adducts provided access to the target DHM enantiomers in 9 steps, with >25% overall yield and >95% ee, starting from thiomethylacetyloxazolidinone. Induced-fit docking studies using the hCYP2B6 crystal structure suggest that both enantiomers of DHM adopt similar binding orientations within the CYP2B6 active site, independent of stereochemistry. In this orientation, the methylenedioxy group is directed toward the heme center and interacts with Thr302, potentially producing a reactive carbene that inhibits CYP2B6 catalytic activity. These computational data are consistent with previously reported in vitro findings and provide insights into DHM–CYP2B6 interactions at the molecular level.

item.title: Nucleophilic Reactions of Cyclobutenones and the Related 4,4‐Dichlorocyclobutenone Derivatives
item.description:
Cyclobutenone derivates and their 4,4-dichloro counterparts have an uninterrupted attention as useful synthons in the synthesis of complex organic molecules. Their nucleophilic reactions remain underexplored. This review brings attention to these reactions, whose outcome is not straightforward. A similar trend is observed with the proposed mechanisms that are used to describe the formation of the observed products.


Cyclobutenones have uninterrupted attention as useful synthons in the synthesis of complex organic molecules. Much of that interest is directed toward strain-release reactions, a result of the inherent ring-strain four-membered ring exacerbated by the embedded enone functionality in the cyclobutenone framework. Little attention is paid to the nucleophilic reactions of the cyclobutenone nucleus and their 4,4-dichloro analogs. These reactions are often found dispersed in literature, and this review is our attempt to bring these reactions to the attention of the synthesis organic chemistry community.

item.title: Base‐Free Nickel‐Catalyzed Three‐Component Coupling of Aldehydes, Butadiene, and Malonate Derivatives: Toward Sustainable Synthesis of Highly Functionalized Molecules
item.description:
A nickel-catalyzed three-component reaction between arylaldehydes, butadiene, and malonates is developed yielding high functionalized homoallylic alcohols in a single step. No additional base is required and the reaction shows broad substrates compatibility with yields up to 96% and an exclusive selectivity toward the linear E-isomer.


We report a nickel-catalyzed multicomponent reaction between benzaldehyde derivatives, butadiene, and various malonates under mild conditions. The protocol provides a straightforward one-step synthesis of homoallylic alcohols functionalized with a double bond and a malonate moiety without the need for any additional base or cocatalyst. The synthesis is highly selective yielding a single E-isomer.

item.title: Electrochemical C–H Nitration of N‐Substituted Anilines With Sodium Nitrite
item.description:
An electrochemical nitration of N-substituted anilines using NaNO2 as the nitro source is developed. The method operates under constant current without external oxidants, catalysts, or additional electrolytes and accommodates a broad range of functional groups. Mechanistic studies support an ionic pathway, and gram-scale synthesis confirms its practical utility.


An environmentally friendly electrochemical nitration of N-substituted anilines using NaNO2 as the nitro source is reported. The method operates under constant current conditions in a CH3CN/H2O solvent mixture without the need for external oxidants, metal catalysts, or additional electrolytes. A wide range of aniline derivatives bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups undergo smooth nitration to afford the corresponding nitroanilines in moderate to excellent yields. Cyclic voltammetry studies reveal that the presence of nitrite facilitates the oxidation of the aniline substrate, while radical trapping experiments support an ionic reaction pathway. The scalability of the protocol is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis. This work provides a sustainable and operationally simple approach to the construction of valuable nitroaniline scaffolds.

item.title: A Highly Selective Indoxyl‐Free Synthesis of Indirubins From Isatins and 2‐Aminoacetophenones via a Knoevenagel Condensation–Cyclization Cascade
item.description:
A base-mediated Knoevenagel condensation–cyclization cascade between isatins and 2-aminoacetophenones/2-aminophenacyl bromides enables the selective synthesis of indirubins. The indoxyl-free process suppresses indigo formation, exhibits broad substrate scope, and provides products under mild, chromatography-free conditions.


A base-mediated condensation of isatins with readily accessible 2-aminoacetophenones or 2-aminophenacyl bromides for the synthesis of indirubins has been realized. In contrast to most reported methods, which proceed through an “indoxyl” intermediate and often generate indigo as a side product via self-dimerization, the present protocol selectively affords (Z)-indirubins, owing to a distinct substrate-specific mechanistic pathway. The method features broad substrate scope, avoids chromatographic purification, and employs commercially available isatins and synthetically accessible 2-aminoacetophenones or 2-aminophenacyl bromides as starting materials, highlighting its practical applicability and synthetic utility.

item.title: Iron‐Catalyzed Hydrodecarboxylation of Fatty Acids From Vegetable Oils for Drop‐In Biofuel Production
item.description:
An iron-catalyzed hydrodecarboxylation for renewable hydrocarbon production is reported, featuring an alternative hydrogen source and a commercially available iron salt as the catalyst. The protocol enabled efficient one-pot C n–1 hydrocarbon synthesis from vegetable oils under mild and open-air conditions.


An iron-catalyzed hydrodecarboxylation procedure was developed to produce drop-in biofuels from redox-active esters directly derived from vegetable oils. A commercially available iron salt, Fe(acac)3, was employed as a homogeneous catalyst, while phenylsilane (PhSiH3) served as an alternative hydrogen source under mild reaction conditions. After optimization, the method enabled the formation of renewable hydrocarbons with conversions exceeding 88% and yields of up to 89%. Furthermore, a one-pot procedure was developed to simplify the overall process. In addition, the methodology was successfully applied to a variety of fatty acid mixtures obtained from a wide range of vegetable oils, affording conversions of 60%–95% and hydrocarbon yields of 15%–94%. This approach represents a promising alternative to traditional deoxygenation processes, promoting the production of biofuels from renewable and feasible feedstocks.

item.title: Copper‐Catalyzed Arylation of Cyclic and Bridged Diamines for Drug Discovery
item.description:
A general, operationally simple copper-catalyzed Chan–Lam amination enables efficient coupling of (hetero)arylboronic acids with diverse cyclic diamines. The method affords pharmaceutically relevant (hetero)aryldiamines in good yields, expanding synthetic options for medicinal chemistry and linker design. Notably, it represents the first Chan–Lam coupling of bridged cyclic diamines, a privileged scaffold for lipophilicity modulation.


Cyclic diamines are a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry, widely used to modulate physicochemical properties and as linker units in bifunctional molecules such as Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras. Existing approaches for aryl functionalization of these motifs rely on SNAr or Buchwald–Hartwig amination, but methods for cyclic and bridged cyclic diamines remain underdeveloped. We report an operationally simple, ligand-free copper-catalyzed Chan–Lam amination that couples arylboronic acids with a broad range of cyclic diamines under mild conditions. The protocol tolerates diverse functional groups, including halides and heteroaryl motifs, delivering pharmaceutically relevant building blocks in good yields. Notably, this strategy enables the first general access to bridged cyclic aryldiamines via Chan–Lam coupling, expanding the scope of this transformation. This method complements existing approaches and provides a practical route to complex diamine architectures for medicinal chemistry applications.
